Axios PM
By Mike Allen · Nov 10, 2026

🚢 Good Tuesday afternoon. We take a moment to remember, on this date in 1975, the sinking of the Great Lakes iron-ore freighter Edmund Fitzgerald in a storm on Lake Superior. The entire crew of 29 perished. Read more.

  • Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 683 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

🏛️ Breaking: House Republicans elected Judiciary Chair Jim Jordan (R-Ohio) as their new leader, handing the reins of the battered GOP conference to one of its most prominent conservative firebrands. Rep. Steve Scalise (R-La.) trailed Jordan by 33 votes in a secret ballot, 106-73. Go deeper.

⚡️ Situational awareness: Caleb Orr will become White House deputy chief of staff for policy, succeeding Stephen Miller, Axios' Alex Isenstadt reports. Orr previously was an adviser in Miller's policy office.
 
 
1 big thing: Hegseth comes out swinging
 
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth holds a press conference at the Pentagon today. Photo: Nathan Howard/AP

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth lambasted Rep. Thomas Massie's (R-Ky.) push to oust him today, Axios' Avery Lotz reports.

  • Massie introduced articles of impeachment against Hegseth yesterday over his handling of the Iran war and other alleged misconduct.

🎤 Hegseth told reporters at the Pentagon this morning: "They impeached President Trump over a perfect phone call. They impeached him again in his final week in office," referencing Trump's first impeachment over a phone call in which he pressed Ukraine to investigate Joe Biden and his second over the Jan. 6 attack.

  • "Both times, he came back stronger, and the American people sent him back to the White House. Now they're trying a third time. This time against a member of his Cabinet."
  • "They will fail again, and if standing with President Trump puts me in that company, I'll take that company every day of the week."

🪖 Hegseth also defended controversial U.S. military operations in Iran, Venezuela and the Caribbean.

  • "We sank the boats carrying poison into our communities. We put a narco dictator in handcuffs. These are not high crimes. This is the job, and it's the job well done."

President Trump gave Hegseth's performance "an 'A' PLUS, PLUS, PLUS" in a Truth Social post.

  • Go deeper.
 
 
2. 📜 MLK draft could fetch $10M
 
Photo: Tony Cenicola/The New York Times

A handwritten draft of Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech is going up for auction in January at Christie's.

  • The document, found in a desk drawer of a former aide, is expected to sell for more than $10 million.

The proceeds will go toward the King Center and other philanthropic causes.

Photo: Christie's

✍️ The seven pages of yellow legal pad paper are believed to be the only surviving handwritten version of King's final draft.

  • Peter Klarnet, Christie's manuscript specialist, told The New York Times: "This is the most important manuscript I've ever had the honor to handle."

Gift link ... Auction details.

Strengthening U.S. competitiveness.

 
 
3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Data: Bureau of Labor Statistics. Chart: Courtenay Brown/Axios
  1. 💸 Inflation stayed hot in October even as gasoline prices steadied (and are now below $4 nationally), per new Labor Department data. More from Courtenay Brown.
  2. 💰 Anthropic is seeking to raise up to $62.5 billion in its IPO at a market cap that could top $1 trillion. That would make it one of the largest IPOs ever, but smaller than some had expected. More from Dan Primack.
  3. 🐘 Sen. Ted Cruz announced a new Austin headquarters for his group Saving Texas, which aims to win back the Lone Star State for Republicans. Cruz said in a statement first provided to Axios: "The work of rebuilding our party begins right here." More from Stef W. Kight.
 
 
4. ✈️ 1 for the road: Dulles sneak peek
 
The new United Club at Dulles Concourse E. Image: United Airlines

Dulles Airport's new Concourse E opens today, bringing United Airlines travelers spacious gates, more concessions and a swanky club lounge, Axios D.C.'s Cuneyt Dil reports after getting a sneak peek yesterday.

  • The project is one step toward Dulles' massive modernization, which will take up to 10 years, phase out "people movers" and add more gates.

🍽️ At yesterday's unveiling, the sleek aesthetics and new food options (we heard one person rave about Bonchon Korean Fried Chicken) got plenty of attention.

  • So did the bathrooms.
Photo: Cuneyt Dil/Axios

🚇 The new United Club lounge has a local nod: The escalator entrance pays homage to the Metro's iconic brutalist stations.

  • Inside, there are two buffet stations, a bar and seating for more than 600 customers.
